Wales: 5 Must-Ride Motorcycle Roads

Wales packs incredible riding into a compact country. These five roads are essential for any British touring rider.

  1. Black Mountain Pass — Brecon Beacons. Wales' finest riding road with dramatic scenery.
  2. Evo Triangle — North Wales. Three roads forming a perfect triangle of fast, technical riding near Betws-y-Coed.
  3. Horseshoe Pass — North Wales. A sweeping mountain road above Llangollen.
  4. A470 Snowdonia — Through the heart of Snowdonia National Park.
  5. A4069 Black Mountain Road — South Wales. As featured on Top Gear.

Total riding: 280+ miles. Best months: April to October. Watch for sheep, single-track roads, and sudden weather changes.
keyTakeaways: Wales packs five essential riding roads into a compact country totalling 280-plus miles.
The Black Mountain Pass in the Brecon Beacons is Wales' finest riding road.
The Evo Triangle near Betws-y-Coed offers fast, technical riding across three linked roads.
The A4069 Black Mountain Road featured on Top Gear for its dramatic switchbacks.
Best riding months are April to October; watch for sheep and sudden weather changes.

faq.q: What is the best motorcycle road in Wales?
faq.a: The Black Mountain Pass in the Brecon Beacons is widely regarded as Wales' finest riding road, combining sweeping bends with dramatic open scenery. The nearby A4069 Black Mountain Road, made famous by Top Gear, is another south Wales highlight with its tight switchbacks. Both reward smooth, flowing riding.

The Evo Triangle is a loop of three linked roads in North Wales near Betws-y-Coed, named after the car magazine that used it for testing. It offers fast, technical riding with a mix of long straights and challenging bends. It is popular, so ride it early or midweek and watch for other enthusiasts and police patrols.

faq.q: How long does it take to ride these Welsh roads?
faq.a: Linking all five roads covers over 280 miles, which makes a full and rewarding day or a relaxed weekend if you stop to enjoy the scenery. Welsh roads are twisty and often single-track, so average speeds are lower than on motorways. Allow plenty of time and build in cafe and fuel stops.

faq.q: When is the best time to ride in Wales?
faq.a: April to October offers the most settled weather and the best chance of dry roads. Welsh mountain weather changes fast, so pack waterproofs whatever the forecast. Avoid the depths of winter, when ice and standing water make the passes hazardous, and ride midweek in summer to avoid tourist traffic.

faq.q: What hazards should I watch for on Welsh roads?
faq.a: Sheep are a constant hazard on unfenced mountain roads and can bolt without warning, so slow down when you see them near the verge. Many roads are single-track with passing places, blind crests are common, and mountain weather can bring sudden rain and fog. Ride within your sight lines and stay alert.
